mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors price in reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: INDPRO declines correlate with positive 20d SPX returns in >60% of instances (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate decline below 4.5% signals monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 4.5% periods yield negative 20d SPX returns in >60% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Joint decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates deteriorating economic conditions, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as recession fears intensify.
failure_condition: INDPRO and PAYEMS decline together but SPX 20d returns are positive in >60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 1200 units signal weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days due to reduced construction sector activity.
failure_condition: HOUST < 1200 periods produce positive 20d SPX returns in >60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Real sales below $370 billion indicate declining consumer demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days as corporate revenue expectations fall.
failure_condition: RSAFS < 370000 periods have positive 60d SPX returns in >60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 209.5 in a high-inflation regime signals monetary policy tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days as real rates rise.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 209.5 periods yield positive 60d SPX returns in >60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in CPI (CPIAUCSL) indicates stagflation, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: INDPRO decline and CPIAUCSL rise together but SPX 20d returns are positive in >60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 4.8% signals labor market deterioration, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days as recession risks accelerate.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 4.8% periods produce positive 5d SPX returns in >60% of cases.
